title: This is my second Asian summer after coming to Seoul
body:
I was on vacation in Tokyo last year. It was so hot that I doubted my life.

I learned a lesson this year and ran directly north.

Hokkaido.

It turns out that maps don’t lie.

When we got off the plane, it was less than twenty degrees.

I forgave Asian Summer on the spot.

Drive all the way from Sapporo to Furano, Biei, Asahikawa, Otaru, and then to Tomakomai.

All the way there is one thing in common, cleanliness.

Very clean.

How clean is it?

I was looking for trash cans all the way.

Later, I discovered that there may not be trash cans, but there really is no garbage.

Not on the roadside, not in the city, not everywhere.

There was another discovery.

Japanese cars are so small.

How small?

Looking from a distance, it looks like a group of small toy cars in cartoons, lining up to go to work seriously.

If an American SUV were parked next to it and it sneezed, three Japanese cars next to it would be ejected.

What’s even more amazing is that I didn’t hear a single car horn during the entire trip.

Not a sound.

I once wondered whether Japanese local cars were not equipped with this function when they left the factory.

Later, while there was no one around, I secretly found a deserted road to verify it.

Found not to be.

It's just that everyone is very patient, a little unhumanly patient. At least not like most American drivers I know, or Korean drivers for that matter...

And air.

There is no smell of smoke at all in the public areas.

I couldn't help but think of the smell that mixes all year round in downtown Seattle.

It's hard to tell whether it's marijuana or homeless people.

Or the homeless man smokes weed and then, like some animals, marks his territory with his "organic shower"...

In comparison, Seoul has done well, with a high concentration of smoking areas. Just when passing by, you are still forced to take a few breaths of other people's lives.

Japan is more direct, preparing a separate small room for smokers.

It's full of smoke inside, but the years are quiet outside.

Smokers smoke their own smoke, and passersby smoke their own smoke.

Don't disturb each other.

The most comfortable relationship for adults is probably like this.

What really impressed me along the way was not the scenery.

It's human

The first time I took a left-hand taxi in Sydney many years ago, it left a bit of a psychological shadow.

This time I decided to challenge my life again.

When I actually drove right-hand drive for the first time, I was still very conservative.

To be precise, very cowardly.

The cars behind me passed one by one from the right.

I was mentally prepared to accept the international practice of being looked down upon and greeted with the same middle finger by American drivers.

It turned out not to be.

When people passed by, they waved to me and nodded.

That means roughly:

"Sorry, I'll go over first."

There is only one sentence in my mind:"Brother, it's obviously me who is slow, why are you still apologizing to me?"

Later, roads were built along the way.

The worker held a soft warning cloth in his hand.

Keep opening and closing.

Open, close.

Like a GIF.

Purely handmade.

No electricity, no AI.

The frame rate is quite high.

They bowed every time a car passed by.

It probably means:

"Sorry, it took you dozens of seconds."

I think they bow hundreds of times a day and their waists are really good.

I suddenly thought of building roads in the United States.

Block one lane and block it for 40 minutes. No explanation, no apology.

Six or seven workers gathered around to watch one man working.

There was another person who held up the stop sign with an expressionless face.

The navigation will only tell you calmly:

"Estimated delay is 38 minutes."

Make it sound like these 38 minutes of self-righteousness never belonged to you.

During breakfast, an old man was responsible for cleaning the table.

Hold the watering can in your left hand and keep it in front of you with your right hand.

Because there were people waiting for a table next to us, we were afraid of water mist splashing on others.

I stared at it for a long time.

Suddenly I felt that a watering can can also be very educational.

Later we went to Furano to buy the local specialty - cantaloupe.

Can't read Japanese.

I picked the one that looked better to me based on my feeling.

When I was checking out, my aunt stopped me and kept gesticulating with me.

My heart tightened, and my first reaction was, it's over. Have you picked out the treasure in the store?

Open Google Translate. She said:

"This one won't be ripe until three days. I guess you want to eat it today."

I nodded as fast as pounding garlic.

Then Auntie led me to another row of shelves.

Picking up a melon that is obviously prettier than me.

Meaning: Eat this one today.

I rushed back to the hotel.

The first thing is to cut the melon.

It's not because of greed, at least not entirely. It's because I'm too curious.

The result was really just right. It's so soft that it melts in your mouth, and it's as sweet as cheating.

For the first time, I learned that cantaloupe has an "appointment to ripen", and it is accurate to the sky.

Later I went to Rokkatei to buy desserts.

When the clerk was checking out, she checked the shelf life of each box.

Then I was reminded: This - Matcha Daifuku, I need to finish it before tomorrow.

I suddenly felt that she knew my eating plan for the next twenty-four hours better than my mother.

Go refuel on the last day.

I stared at a bunch of Japanese buttons and studied them for a long time, but I still didn't understand them.

The gas station boy had already ran all the way out of the hut.

Not a fast walk, but a real run.

At that speed, it seems that if I were slower for one second, I would blow up the gas station.

He helped me fill up the tank. He kept apologizing to me in broken English because he was worried that I would wait too long.

It made me very embarrassed.

All the way down.There is no earth-shattering event, no movie plot, and no conclusion of "what are the Japanese like?"

Just a lot of people,

Be willing to go the extra mile.

One more reminder.

Take two more steps.

Block the spray more.

Take one more bow.

These actions were so small that I thought they would be forgotten five minutes later.

But after the trip, all I remembered was these.

Later I discovered that the most interesting part of traveling is never seeing anything. But after I came back, I started to learn something secretly.

For example, if I pass a car that is driving slowly in the future, I will no longer honk my horn.

I might wave my hand,

Tell him:

It doesn't matter,

Slower, that's fine too.

title: F. William Sunderman - The Invisible Threads of a Life.
body:
From Tuberculosis Research to eCommerce: How Unexpected Encounters Reveal the Threads That Connect a Life

It’s graduation season, and an email from the University of Toronto alumni office unexpectedly found its way into my inbox, calling me back to the campus to celebrate. Like many alumni messages, it was meant to celebrate new beginnings. Yet instead, it quietly transported me back to my own graduate days, when I was immersed in tuberculosis research and thought my future would remain firmly rooted in molecular biology and microbiology.

Life, of course, had other plans.

Over the years, I have wandered through sales, stem cells, real estate, insurance, cooking, archery, skiing, scuba diving, and eventually eCommerce. Looking back, I sometimes wonder how these seemingly disparate chapters could possibly belong to the same story.Perhaps it was nostalgia, but this afternoon, while browsing through Kyobo Book Center in Gangnam, a book on the history of laboratory medicine caught my attention. As I leafed through its pages, one name stood out: F. William Sunderman.

Most remember him as the physician-scientist who pioneered proficiency testing and helped establish the standards upon which modern laboratory medicine depends. What fascinated me even more was that he was also an accomplished violinist. Having survived tuberculosis himself, he practiced music daily and continued both working and performing well past his hundredth birthday. His life was not a straight line, but a remarkable tapestry of science, art, discipline, and resilience.

The more I read about him, the more I understood why his story resonated with me.The precision he pursued in laboratories reminds me of the standards I strive for in business. His love of music echoes the joy I find in wine tasting, cooking and sports. His encounter with tuberculosis brings me back to my years at the bench. And his lifelong willingness to transcend disciplines and reinvent himself resonates deeply as I continue to navigate among science, commerce, and creativity.

Over time, I have come to appreciate that life is seldom linear. What appear to be detours are often tributaries flowing toward the same sea. Curiosity, precision, and resilience may take different forms, but their essence remains unchanged.

Perhaps passion never truly expires; it simply finds new expressions. And perhaps reinvention is not a departure from who we are, but a deeper return to it.Sometimes, the most meaningful encounters happen quietly - an email from an alma mater, an unplanned afternoon in a bookstore, and the unexpected discovery of a life that, in some small way, helps us understand our own.

title: The sound of cicadas remains the same every year, the sound is not that of an old friend
body:
I went downstairs to exercise and met two cicadas today.

The first one was green, lying motionless on the cement floor. I picked it up and put it on a nearby tree. It quickly inserted its mouthparts into the bark and started sucking the sap. It seemed like he was just too weak.

After walking a few more steps, I met another one.

It had just finished eclosion, but not entirely successfully. One wing was still stuck to the old shell and rolled into a ball, and it couldn't be shaken off no matter how hard it struggled. I slowly separated the wings from the old shell, trying not to hurt them, and found some water, hoping that the wings could still stretch.

Unfortunately, it was too late.

I changed a few trees and put it on the trunk. It always slides down after only a few steps, lying on its back on the ground to rest. I didn't leave, I just sat next to it and waited for it to calm down before putting it back on the trunk.

fall down.

Put it on again.

Fall again.

Put it on again.

I don't know how long it took, but it finally firmly grasped the bark of the tree.

There was no rush to rush up, just small steps to climb up.

At that moment, I suddenly remembered the sentence in "Jurassic Park":

Life finds a way.

Later, I checked and found out that after living underground for three to five years, the real time for sunshine is only one summer.

When we study medicine, we are always accustomed to understanding life from the perspective of species.

It failed to emerge and could not reproduce. From the perspective of natural selection, it probably could no longer complete its mission of continuing genes.

But while squatting under the tree to accompany it, I suddenly felt that species and individuals are originally two different perspectives.

Natural selection cares about continuation.

What matters in life may just be living.

If it cannot leave its own DNA in the end, at least it has crawled out of the darkness, grabbed a tree, blown the summer wind, and heard its own cicada chirp.

I continue to go to the gym.

He glanced back.

It's still climbing slowly.

title: St. Louis left two deepest impressions on me
body:
One is the weather.

Summer temperatures can reach 40 degrees Celsius, making it breathless. In spring, tornado warnings are almost a daily occurrence. When sirens sound throughout the city, everyone hides in the basement. Cars were rolled onto roofs, and hailstones as big as baseballs were commonplace...

The other is people.

After working there for several years, many of the people I met were very simple and pure. This ratio, at least in other places in the United States that I later visited, was not that high.

Today I received an email about the 25th anniversary of Give Kids a Smile, and I was reminded of one of them - Dr. Jeff Dalin.

More than ten years ago, I was working at Sigma-Aldrich and in my spare time I was seriously preparing to apply to dental school. I volunteer at Give Kids a Smile on the weekends. At that time, the entire project was almost solely by Jeff, plus a few of our volunteers, providing free oral examinations and teeth cleanings to children from low-income families. Naturally, Jeff and I became lifelong friends.

Later, I returned to the West Coast and helped raise funds for a period of time, hoping to bring this project there. However, the medical environment and family conditions in different regions vary greatly, and in the end it was not really implemented.

Time has passed, and today I saw that Give Kids a Smile has reached its 25th anniversary, and I also noticed that Jeff won the ADA Humanitarian Award four years ago.

Persisting in doing a seemingly ordinary thing well is actually not easy. Very happy for them

title: Four o'clock Michelin
body:
End of Q2. I only went out to play for more than two weeks.

Meeting in the first week back.

There is only one theme, employee bonus.

hair.

Still not posting.

I've always felt that.

It's not that complicated.

The work is done, the money is given to them, and the meeting is dismissed.

As a result, more than a dozen people. The discussion lasted two hours.

Finally, he actually asked me:

“What would you think if your employees weren’t given bonuses?”

What do I think? ! I cover my eyes and watch

Failure to protect your own employees is like a parent unable to protect your children.

Quite uncomfortable.

What's even more uncomfortable is that this topic can still be discussed.

I sat there, as if thinking. But it looks more like sleeping.

Look at the mouths in the conference room that are still talking.

I suddenly felt very sleepy and couldn't help but want to yawn.

It's not very polite in front of so many people. I can only hold it in.

As a result, the yawn did not come out and turned into a burp.

The hiccup went all the way up my throat, and I swallowed it back.

This swallow made me hold back two lines of tears.

I was about to wipe it off naturally when the person next to me who was still speaking passionately suddenly glanced at me.

I can't forget that expression to this day. As if thinking "Is this topic...so sad?"

Or: "What are you unhappy about? Tell me about it to make everyone happy?"

After two hours, there will be no conclusion. My battery ran out first.

I open Outlook. I wanted to see if I could be any more unlucky today.

As a result, I have a holiday tomorrow.

I don’t know what festival it is in Korea, and it doesn’t matter.

As long as you have a holiday, it's a good holiday. I did not hesitate to cancel the afternoon meeting.

Today, stop being a human being. Go out and forage like a wild animal.

When you feel bad, look for food! Especially meaningful. At least half an hour of fun.

I wandered all the way to Insadong. This is a place that has a little bit of everything.

There are people selling calligraphy and paintings, dragon beard candy, comics, seals, Korean souvenirs, and many other things that I don’t know what they sell, but they look good to buy.

It is very close to Gyeongbokgung Palace and there are many foreigners. It is a bit like the Korean version of Wangfujing. It's just proportionally smaller based on the land area.

As I walked, I turned into a very Korean alley.

Suddenly I found a line of people in front of me.

Life experience in Asia tells me that the length of the queue is the most useful Dianping.

I hesitated for a second.

First in line or first to see.

In the end, curiosity won.

I ran to the door and took a look. dumpling? That's it? What’s so great about dumplings?

Looking to the side, Michelin! For several years in a row! My pupils instantly dilated six times.

Suddenly, I am no longer sleepy or tired. The meeting in the morning was not that annoying anymore.God is still fair. He wanted to take away my employee bonus in the morning and pay me a Michelin in the afternoon.

Satisfied, I started to line up, and the line in front of me was getting shorter and shorter.

Behind me, there was no one.

I'm still a little proud. It seems that there are not many people as smart as me.

Finally, it's my turn. I just stepped in with one leg.

An aunt, standard Japanese and Korean gestures. Cross your arms.

❌

Then he yelled at me: "Aniu...Mida..."

I was stunned. Look down at yourself. Crocs. Although it's a little casual.

Could it be...eat a dumpling and dress code?

I have been in Korea for a year and a half, and my Korean level is not much better than a humane wild dog on the roadside.

Auntie looked at me dumbfounded and pointed to the opening hours at the door.

Oh, and it closes at 2 p.m.

I looked down at my watch. One sixty.

At this time, the aunt said something again.

I finally understood that it was not me who was late, but the foot I had just put in that prevented her from closing the door.

I pulled my foot back.

The door, the moment my feet left. "Click." It closed.

It's as precise as NASA launching a rocket.

I finally understood why there was no one in line behind me just now.

I looked up at the opening hours again. The doors reopen at 4 p.m.

Two hours left. Two hours.

Time is so precious, you can't waste two hours just because of greed.

I stood at the door. Think seriously for three seconds.

Then, not surprisingly.

Decide to wait.

Think positively about everything. Two hours later, I was one of the first customers of the day. Muhahahaha.

However, just standing at the door looks too much like a beggar.

Squatting, more like squatting to beg for food.

Still, let’s take a walk around first.

Anyway, the lunch meal is definitely not as delicious as the evening meal.

For sure. Must.

I started brainwashing myself and it worked.

However, the weather is still hot. Want to buy something to eat?

no.

That four-point Michelin is so ungrateful.

You can drink water, I bought a bottle. Tons tons tons.

Still hot.

There happened to be a small studio nearby with air conditioning. I walked in without hesitation.

It’s not for art, it’s for air-conditioning. I don’t draw much.

In order to stay a little longer, I decided to seriously appreciate art.

I stood for a long time on each painting. After a long time, others should think that this is a person who knows how to draw.

Actually, I just want to blow the air conditioner for two more minutes.

Looking at it, I feel thirsty again. Go out and buy another bottle of water, tons, tons, tons.

Come back and work on the next painting.

I feel like I am not coming to see paintings, but more like doing intermittent irrigation for the gallery.The boss at the door began to salute me with his eyes, and his eyes became more and more complex.

I guess he was probably thinking: "Why does this foreigner like my paintings so much? Why does he run out every time he looks at them? Come back and continue looking at them?"

Finally. He couldn't help it. Give me a Korean output.

It should be introducing paintings, it might be introducing painters, it might also be introducing prices.

I didn't understand a word of it, but I smiled politely. Keep nodding.

When a person doesn't speak a foreign language, nod. Always the safest answer.

In order to avoid further communication, I began to move slowly inside. Move all the way to the painting in the far corner. Not because it's the best, not because it's the biggest.

It's just that the boss can't see me from that position. Air conditioning is the coolest.

Moreover, I was too hungry to walk.

Time passed very slowly, and finally, it was almost four o'clock.

I looked at my phone and saw that it was 3:50 and it was time to leave.

When I went out, I was a little embarrassed. Bowed to the boss. After looking at paintings for so long, I didn’t buy any. I always feel like an art thief.

I trotted all the way to the Michelin restaurant.

The alley is quiet. Sure enough, I was the first.

As soon as I stood up, people suddenly started growing behind me.

one. two. Five. Ten.

Like a magnet, people appear out of nowhere.

Does everyone know that the door opens on time at four o'clock?

3:55.

I don’t know if it’s because I’m excited, or if I just drank two bottles of water too seriously. I suddenly wanted to go to the toilet, and the problem came.

If I go and come back now, I won’t be number one.

If I didn’t go, I might immediately become the most famous person in Insadong.

I stood there, thinking seriously for the first time in my life. Which is more important, the stomach or the bladder?

Five minutes left, will they open on time? What if "wait a moment" is also popular among Koreans?

Just when my two organs were pulling against each other,

door

It's open.

The aunt who blocked me out just now recognized me at a glance and was obviously stunned.

That expression seemed to say: "This fool...actually waited for two hours?"

The next second, she smiled. Wave to me, come in.

It was no longer a wave, it was a door. A gleaming golden light leads to the door to heaven.

I flew in with a "swish". As they approached, the aunt at the door was stunned for a moment. Did any large creature fly past just now?

I didn't care so much and rushed towards a door inside.

Finally, I found the toilet... I opened the door, and it was not a toilet.

Kitchen.

The two chefs stopped what they were doing at the same time and looked at me. I looked at them too. The air was suddenly quiet.

Three seconds later. The entire kitchen erupted at the same time:

"Get out!"I bowed all the way. Exit backwards.

At that moment, I felt. All the Korean I know in my life is in my mouth.

I finally found the real bathroom, and when I came out, I lost half my weight.

Finally, I can order food without any burden.

The restaurant is not big, with seven or eight tables. The people in line behind me have already filled all the tables.

I opened the menu and there weren't many dishes. Meat dumplings. Kimchi dumplings. Mushroom dumplings.

Then, there are meat dumplings, kimchi dumplings, mushroom dumplings, and different amounts of permutations and combinations.

Seeing this, I suddenly thought of my dad. There are four of his best dishes:

Stir-fried eggs with tomatoes, stir-fry tomatoes with eggs, stir-fry tomatoes with eggs, stir-fry eggs with tomatoes.

The menu is like this. Then I'll simply have one of each. Experience it. In the costume drama, the emperor's joy of flipping brands is soaked in rain and dew.

The waiter stood nearby waiting for me to take my order.

I pointed with my fingers all the way from top to bottom. Clicked them all.

He kept looking at my hands. I guess I'm waiting to see where I end up.

result. I pointed again from the beginning. For each finger, I raised a finger in the air, "One."

Fingers are truly mankind’s greatest invention. It can express both direction and quantity. Especially suitable for illiterate people like me.

The waiter began to hesitate. Look at the menu and look at me.

Then, I took a pen and drew a circle on the menu. It probably means: "Want them all?"

"Guilty!"

I spoke Korean as loud as I could in my life and nodded vigorously.

He still looked worried and confirmed again.

I almost laughed. I'm a grown man. I come to Michelin and just order a plate of dumplings. Is that right?

So, I simply opened my hands. In the air, a huge circle was drawn.

All.

all.

Don't leave any one behind.

The waiter finally said OK and slowly walked back to the kitchen. However, when I walked to the door, I couldn't help but look back at me. Then, he whispered a few words to another person in the kitchen.

I guess they were probably discussing: "How many days has this foreigner not eaten?"

After a while, a pile of steel bowls and plates were brought up first.

Pickles, and several dishes of liquid that I had no idea what it was. But you can roughly judge from the size that the big bowl is soup and the small dish is dipping sauce.

The Korean dining table sometimes resembles a chemistry laboratory. The reagents are put in place first, and the protagonist appears last.

After waiting for a while, the waiter came over with the first plate of dumplings.

As soon as the plate was placed on the table, I was stunned for a moment.

What is this?

on the plate

standing group

Something about the size of a fist.

Judging by the shape, you can’t tell it’s not a dumpling.

With skin,

There is stuffing,It is indeed closed tightly and feels very safe.

But this size is obviously not the same species as the familiar dumplings in my mind.

Ostrich is also a bird, hummingbird is also a bird. But you can't let them sit on the same table just because they both have wings.

I'm still in a daze.

The second set is coming.

Then.

The third set also came.

Three plates of dumplings.

Neatly.

Instantly occupying the entire table, like a group of sumo wrestlers.

Sitting there one after another, they were fat, big, stable, and full of momentum.

I looked up at the waiter. That look was probably asking: "You call these dumplings?"

He looked at me without explaining. Just follow the way I ordered the food just now. He stretched out his hand and slowly drew a large circle in the air.

Want them all. Right? Finished painting.

He nodded proudly, turned around and left.

I suddenly understood that he didn't understand just now. He listened very well.

People at several tables around me also started to look at me.

Look at the table first, then at me, then at the table.

There was surprise, admiration, and a little worry in those eyes.

Probably thinking: Is there a beggar living in this person's belly?

I was silent, but only for a moment.

I remembered the heroic past when I walked into the Mandarin to eat at the buffet while holding on to the wall, and then walked out holding on to the wall.

I wasn't even afraid at that time.

Today, isn’t it just a few plates of dumplings? And, it’s Michelin.

I can.

I picked one up.

First reaction.

So heavy.

The chopsticks dropped slightly, like picking up a small piece of fitness equipment.

I adjusted my wrist, brought it to my mouth, and took a bite.

Um?

I stopped.

Tasteless.

It’s not that it’s not delicious.

It's not unpalatable either.

That is,

No taste.

Like a ball of air wrapped very seriously.

Just to make sure it wasn't my taste buds that were the problem, I took another bite.

After two mouthfuls, my mouth was already full. Like a chipmunk with too many peanuts in its mouth.

I choked and had to rush to find water, tons, tons, tons. It was hard to swallow.

I thought about it carefully again, what did I taste just now?

The answer is.

There is no answer.

Is this Michelin?

You can tell it's not a dumpling, it has stuffing inside and skin on the outside.

They really cooked it for you.

But you call it Michelin.

Where's the salt? Michelin restaurant salt. Are they sold by nanograms?

The big dumpling I bit open, with its chest open and its stuffing exposed. Sitting on the plate looking at me as if smiling.

Come on, continue.

I don't believe in evil. After all, quality inspection also pays attention to random sampling. Just because one of them is tasteless doesn't mean the whole batch is wronged.

I substituted a kimchi filling.

Take a bite.

Tasteless.

Replace the mushroom filling.Still tasteless.

I tried the meat filling again.

Still tasteless.

The three kinds of fillings were all eaten to the same standard.

This is great.

In ordinary restaurants, different fillings taste different.

Michelin can make them taste the same. To be precise, none of them tasted good.

I bit into two of each filling.

The dumplings were too big and I was almost full before the quality inspection was over.

I looked up and looked around. Everyone was eating peacefully. There were no surprises, no frowns, and no one stared at the dumplings doubting life like me.

Looking at their table, the total size of the family is less than half of mine.

I finally understood why the waiter had to confirm so many times just now.

It's not that he looks down on me, it's that he wants to save me.

But again and again, I used my fingers, nodded, and used that huge circle. He firmly rejected his kindness.

What to do with so many untouched dumplings?

I started trying to find reasons for them.

Is it organic?

Is it healthy?

Do Koreans think that adding too much salt can lead to high blood pressure?

Or maybe Michelin has reached a stage where it has long disdained the low-level taste of seasoning.

The more I think about it, the more I feel that they must have their reasons. It’s just that I haven’t reached that level yet.

The group of dumplings on the table stood quietly. Like a group of winning terracotta warriors.

I look at them. They looked at me too. No one gave in first.

But my stomach surrendered first. I put down my chopsticks and finally admitted that today, they were the winners.

I waved and called the waiter over. He pointed at the dumplings on the table, pointed outside, and then made a gesture of putting them into the bag.

Packing, I don’t know this Korean language. But waiters around the world understand it.

He nodded and finally showed his most relaxed expression today. As if to say: "I knew it."

Not long after, a big bag of dumplings came back to me.

Shen.

Extremely heavy.

Carrying it in your hand is not like packing dinner, but like carrying a dumbbell that you just finished working out.

I walked out of the alley carrying it. Suddenly I remembered that today, it seemed that everything was different from what I expected.

I was expecting Q2 employees to get bonuses, but they’re gone.

I was looking forward to seeing a surprise in the afternoon, but ended up being rejected first.

After waiting for two hours, I finally got a Michelin meal.

As a result, I ended up with a table of tasteless Big Mac dumplings.

Life is interesting sometimes. You expect it to go left and it goes right. You feel that the next second is going to take a turn, and it turns another corner for you.

The day is over. After twists and turns, the discount is quite cheap.

Back home.

I looked at the heavy bag of dumplings and remembered what Buffett said: If you want to be happier, expect less.

I think what he said makes sense. At least, it makes sense today.I silently carried the bag of Michelin Big Mac dumplings downstairs.

Swipe your card, open the organic bin, and throw it in.

"Drip."

Deduction successful.

I stood there in silence for two seconds.

The last surprise today

To throw away the unpalatable Michelin, they actually charge a fee.
